correctness.rationale: At round 1 the signature distinguishes the marked origin, identifies b by degree d+b and detects adjacency to the mark. Coordinate permutations preserve all signatures, so each (b,c) type is indivisible. From round t to t+1, in any fixed-b unreached class at most one type can have distance t+1; it alone sees a reached colour. All types at distance >t+1 have exclusively unreached neighbours, with d−b in the b+1 tail and 2b in the b−1 tail (zero-count tails are irrelevant), independently of c. Old colours prevent merging. The final two b=0 types at distances 2d−2 and 2d are still tied at 2d−3, including d=2; at 2d−2 all tails contain at most one type. No earlier equality could precede a later split. Root distance and degree are rooted-automorphism invariants and determine (b,c); coordinate permutations give transitivity on each type. The multinomial size and triangular count follow. The stronger proof statement about the full stabilizer is also sound: degree distinguishes 2e_i among the distance-two neighbours of e_i, and the difference of distances to 2e_i and to the origin determines x_i.
residual_risks: The bounded computation is corroboration only; the induction proves the dimension-uniform result. No formal verification is claimed.

value.rationale: This is a natural controlled family for distinguishing propagation from convergence. The formula tells exactly which types remain indistinguishable after any fixed number of rounds, and shows that orbit separation can finish two rounds before the distance-to-mark signal could reach the far corner. Eventual orbit identification alone does not give either fact.
residual_risks: This is a benchmark for single-corner marking on P3 powers, not a general product-depth or graph-identification theorem.
